questions.prompt: Who appoints the Prime Minister after a general election?
questions.explanation: The monarch appoints as Prime Minister the person most likely to command the confidence of the House of Commons.

questions.prompt: Which part of Parliament is made up of elected MPs?
questions.explanation: Members of Parliament (MPs) are elected to the House of Commons, which is the elected chamber of Parliament.

questions.prompt: Which document from 1215 is often linked with limits on royal power?
questions.explanation: Magna Carta was agreed in 1215 and is associated with limiting the power of the monarch.

questions.prompt: What is one responsibility of people living in the UK?
questions.explanation: Everyone living in the UK is expected to obey the law, whether they are a British citizen or not.

questions.prompt: What event is remembered on Remembrance Day?
options: The service and sacrifice of people in wars
The start of the school year
questions.explanation: Remembrance Day (11 November) honours those who served and died in wars and conflicts, especially the First and Second World Wars.

questions.prompt: Which city is the capital of Wales?
questions.explanation: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales and the seat of the Senedd (Welsh Parliament).

questions.prompt: At what age can most citizens vote in UK general elections?
questions.explanation: Most British citizens can vote in UK general elections from age 18, provided they are registered to vote.

questions.prompt: Which service provides healthcare funded mainly through taxation?
questions.explanation: The National Health Service (NHS) provides healthcare that is mainly funded through taxation.

questions.prompt: Which of these is one of the four countries of the UK?
questions.explanation: The United Kingdom is made up of four countries: England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

questions.prompt: Which flower is commonly associated with Remembrance?
questions.explanation: The red poppy is the main symbol of Remembrance and is worn around Remembrance Day.

questions.prompt: Where does the UK Parliament meet?
questions.explanation: The UK Parliament meets at the Palace of Westminster, often called the Houses of Parliament, in London.

questions.prompt: What type of trial uses a jury in serious criminal cases?
questions.explanation: Serious criminal cases can be heard in the Crown Court, where a jury of members of the public decides the verdict.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a fundamental British value?
options: Democracy and the rule of law
questions.explanation: Fundamental British values include democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance.

questions.prompt: What is the currency of the UK?
questions.explanation: The currency of the UK is the pound sterling, often written as GBP or shown with the £ symbol.

questions.prompt: In which year did the Norman invasion (Battle of Hastings) take place?
questions.explanation: The Norman invasion of England, including the Battle of Hastings, took place in 1066.

questions.prompt: Who wrote 'Romeo and Juliet' and 'Hamlet'?
questions.explanation: William Shakespeare wrote many of the most famous plays in the English language.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in the UK?
questions.explanation: Ben Nevis, in the Scottish Highlands, is the highest mountain in the United Kingdom.

questions.prompt: Which king established the Church of England?
questions.explanation: Henry VIII broke from Rome and established the Church of England in the 16th century.

questions.prompt: Which report led to the creation of the modern welfare state?
questions.explanation: The 1942 Beveridge Report recommended major social reforms and helped shape the modern welfare state, including the NHS.

questions.prompt: How often are general elections required to be held, at most?
questions.explanation: Under current UK law, a general election must be held at least every five years.

questions.prompt: Who is the patron saint of England?
questions.explanation: St George is the patron saint of England; his day is celebrated on 23 April.

questions.prompt: The Industrial Revolution is most associated with developments in which industry first?
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution began with mechanisation of the textile industry in the 18th century.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum age to stand as an MP in the UK?
questions.explanation: Since 2006, people aged 18 or over can stand for election as a Member of Parliament.

questions.prompt: Which of these describes the UK's system of government?
options: A parliamentary democracy and constitutional monarchy
questions.explanation: The UK is a parliamentary democracy and a constitutional monarchy: elected politicians run government, while the monarch is head of state.

questions.prompt: Who is the head of state in the UK?
options: The Speaker of the House of Commons
questions.explanation: The monarch is the UK head of state, while elected politicians run the government.

questions.prompt: Where is the official London residence and office of the Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: 10 Downing Street in London is the official residence and office of the UK Prime Minister.

questions.prompt: What do MPs in the House of Commons do?
options: Represent their constituents and make laws
questions.explanation: MPs represent their constituencies, debate issues, scrutinise government, and vote on new laws.

questions.prompt: Which part of Parliament can review and suggest changes to bills?
questions.explanation: The House of Lords reviews legislation from the Commons and can suggest amendments, but the Commons has the final say on most bills.

questions.prompt: What does the rule of law mean?
questions.explanation: The rule of law means that laws apply equally to everyone, including government and public officials, and no one is above the law.

questions.prompt: What is the number for the police when it is not an emergency?
questions.explanation: 101 is used to contact the police for non-emergency matters. In an emergency, call 999 or 112.

questions.prompt: What should you normally do if you are called for jury service?
options: Attend unless you are formally excused
Ask your MP to decide the case
questions.explanation: Jury service is a civic responsibility, and people called should attend unless excused.

questions.prompt: Which freedom is protected in the UK?
options: Freedom to practise or change your religion
Freedom to stop other people voting
questions.explanation: People in the UK have freedom of religion, including the right to practise or change their religion.

questions.prompt: What is the usual minimum legal age to buy alcohol in the UK?
questions.explanation: In the UK, the usual minimum legal age to buy alcohol from shops, pubs, and bars is 18.

questions.prompt: Which city is the capital of Scotland?
questions.explanation: Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland and the location of the Scottish Parliament.

questions.prompt: Which city is the capital of Northern Ireland?
questions.explanation: Belfast is the capital city of Northern Ireland and the largest city in Northern Ireland.

questions.prompt: Which city is the capital of England?
questions.explanation: London is the capital of England and of the United Kingdom as a whole.

questions.prompt: What is a referendum?
options: A public vote on a specific question
questions.explanation: A referendum is a public vote in which people decide a specific question directly, rather than through elected representatives.

questions.prompt: Which is one way citizens can take part in UK democracy?
questions.explanation: Voting in elections is one of the main ways citizens take part in UK democracy.

questions.prompt: Which organisation gives free, confidential advice on problems such as debt or housing?
questions.explanation: Citizens Advice offers free, confidential, and independent advice on issues such as debt, housing, benefits, and employment.

questions.prompt: What is one common way people contribute to their local community?
options: Volunteering for charities or community groups
Leaving all decisions to the police
questions.explanation: Volunteering is a common way people contribute to local communities, charities, and public services.

questions.prompt: What is the longest river in the UK?
questions.explanation: The River Severn is the longest river in the United Kingdom, flowing through Wales and England.

questions.prompt: Which body of water separates England from France?
questions.explanation: The English Channel is the body of water that separates southern England from northern France.

questions.prompt: What are the Proms?
options: A summer season of classical music concerts
questions.explanation: The Proms are a famous annual season of classical music concerts, best known for the Last Night of the Proms.

questions.prompt: What does mutual respect and tolerance mean?
options: Respecting people with different beliefs and opinions
Only accepting people who agree with you
Letting the government choose your friends
questions.explanation: Mutual respect and tolerance means respecting people who have different beliefs, cultures, and opinions.

questions.prompt: Which British value supports people expressing their opinions peacefully?
questions.explanation: Individual liberty includes the freedom to hold and express opinions within the law.

questions.prompt: Which government body collects Income Tax and National Insurance?
questions.explanation: HM Revenue and Customs collects taxes, including Income Tax and National Insurance.

questions.prompt: What is the National Minimum Wage?
options: The legal minimum hourly pay for most workers
A tax paid only by companies
A fee for using the NHS
questions.explanation: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum hourly pay rate that most workers must receive.

questions.prompt: What do people usually need before starting paid work in the UK?
options: A passport from every UK nation
questions.explanation: People usually need a National Insurance number for work, tax, and benefit records.

questions.prompt: What is the Cabinet in UK government?
options: A group of senior ministers chosen by the Prime Minister
The jury in a Crown Court trial
The staff of the House of Lords
questions.explanation: The Cabinet is made up of senior government ministers, usually chosen by the Prime Minister, who take major decisions together.

questions.prompt: What is a constituency?
options: An area of the country that elects one MP
A tax paid by employers only
A seat in the House of Lords
questions.explanation: A constituency is a geographical area that elects one Member of Parliament to the House of Commons.

questions.prompt: What should you do in a genuine emergency that needs the police, fire, or ambulance service?
questions.explanation: In a genuine emergency, call 999 or 112 so the police, fire, or ambulance service can respond quickly.

questions.prompt: Which of these is both a right and a responsibility in UK society?
options: Looking after the environment and public spaces
Refusing to register to vote when eligible
questions.explanation: People in the UK have responsibilities as well as rights, including looking after the environment and treating public spaces with care.

questions.prompt: Which conflict is particularly remembered each year on Remembrance Day?
questions.explanation: Remembrance Day is especially linked to the First World War, though it also honours those who died in later conflicts.

questions.prompt: Which body makes laws for Scotland on many devolved matters?
questions.explanation: The Scottish Parliament in Edinburgh makes laws on many devolved matters such as education and health in Scotland.

questions.prompt: What is meant by a secret ballot?
options: Votes are cast privately so others cannot see how someone voted
Results of elections are never published
People must tell their employer how they voted
questions.explanation: A secret ballot means people vote in private, so no one else can see or pressure them about their choice.

questions.prompt: What is one important role of charities in the UK?
options: Supporting people and communities, often with volunteer help
questions.explanation: Charities play a major role in UK society by supporting people and communities, often with the help of volunteers and donations.

questions.prompt: Which capital city is furthest north?
questions.explanation: Among the four UK capital cities, Edinburgh is the furthest north, ahead of Belfast, Cardiff, and London.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a famous annual British sporting event?
options: The Tour de France finish in Paris only
questions.explanation: Wimbledon is a famous annual tennis championship held in London and is one of the best-known British sporting events.

questions.prompt: What does individual liberty mean as a British value?
options: People are free to make choices about their lives within the law
Only the government can choose a person's religion
People may ignore criminal laws they dislike
Only one political party may campaign
questions.explanation: Individual liberty means people are free to make their own choices about work, belief, and lifestyle, as long as they stay within the law.

questions.prompt: What is Income Tax mainly used for?
options: Funding public services such as the NHS, schools, and the police
questions.explanation: Income Tax is a major source of government revenue used to fund public services such as healthcare, education, and policing.
